title: Quantification of Medical Waste and Incineration-Related CO 2  Emissions Associated With Gastrointestinal Endoscopy at Two Facilities in Japan: A Preliminary Observational Study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Quantification of Medical Waste and Incineration-Related CO 2  Emissions Associated With Gastrointestinal Endoscopy at Two Facilities in Japan: A Preliminary Observational Study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · deo270455-sec-0050-p1】Climate change increasingly threatens global health. Paradoxically, healthcare also contributes substantially to greenhouse gas emissions through energy consumption, transportation, and the generation of medical waste [1]. Japan, with a rapidly aging population, has had difficulty maintaining a sustainable healthcare system, and its government has set targets to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 46% from 2013 levels by 2030 and to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 [2].

【Introduction · deo270455-sec-0050-p2】Gastrointestinal endoscopy (GIE), one of the most frequently performed examinations at healthcare facilities, represents the third largest source of hospital‐activity‐related medical waste [3]; disposable devices are widely used in GIE to maintain sterility and safety [4]. However, the high daily volume of procedures (e.g., esophagogastroduodenoscopy [EGD] and colonoscopy [CS]) means that the cumulative environmental burden of GIE is considerable. Therefore, “green endoscopy” was introduced by the European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy and other organizations to promote environmentally sustainable endoscopic practices through initiatives such as carbon footprint assessment, waste reduction, and workflow optimization [5].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Quantification of Medical Waste and Incineration-Related CO 2  Emissions Associated With Gastrointestinal Endoscopy at Two Facilities in Japan: A Preliminary Observational Study》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Survey Methodology · deo270455-sec-0070-p3】For each audited procedure, the duration from the endoscope's insertion to its complete withdrawal was recorded using a digital timer, and the medical waste was weighed on a calibrated electronic scale with a readability of 2 g, at the level of aggregation described in the next paragraph. Waste was categorized as infectious (combustible and non‐combustible), non‐infectious (combustible and non‐combustible), liquid (such as suctioned fluids), and sharps or other materials designated for a landfill. Each category was quantified separately; liquid waste was recorded by volume and converted to mass, assuming a density of 1 g/mL. Infectious waste comprised waste contaminated with patients’ body fluids; non‐infectious waste included packaging materials for medical devices. All the disposable items used or generated during each procedure were collected and weighed (e.g., biopsy forceps, sheaths, snares, knives, syringes, gauze, drapes, and disposal bags). Personal protective equipment used outside the procedure room was not included.

【Survey Methodology · deo270455-sec-0070-p1】Surveys were undertaken between June 2024 and January 2025 at a secondary medical institution (Kagawa Rosai Hospital) and a university hospital (Kagawa University Hospital) in Japan. A total of 137 GIEs were audited: 131 at Kagawa Rosai Hospital (79 EGDs, 38 CSs, 10 endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatographies [ERCPs], and four endoscopic submucosal dissections [ESDs]) and six ESDs at Kagawa University Hospital, making ESDs the only type of procedure measured at both institutions.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Quantification of Medical Waste and Incineration-Related CO 2  Emissions Associated With Gastrointestinal Endoscopy at Two Facilities in Japan: A Preliminary Observational Study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Estimated per-procedure CO2 emissions are 949, 1178, 5834, and 4780 g for EGD, CS, ESD, and ERCP, respectively. Aggregate per-minute emissions are 168, 165, 89, and 75 g/min for ERCP, EGD, CS, and ESD, respectively. Annual institutional emissions total approximately 5800 kg. Estimated emissions are 64%-69% and 123%-134% of the base composition scenario values in the lower- and higher-emission composition scenarios, respectively.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】ESD had the highest per-procedure emissions, and ERCP and EGD had the highest per-minute emissions. These results provide preliminary baseline data on incineration-derived CO2 emissions as a foundation for promoting "green endoscopy."

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Quantification of Medical Waste and Incineration-Related CO 2  Emissions Associated With Gastrointestinal Endoscopy at Two Facilities in Japan: A Preliminary Observational Study》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · deo270455-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Medical waste generated during a representative endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD).

【TABLE 1 · deo270455-tbl-0001】TABLE 1 Waste (g) and estimated CO2 emissions (g) generated per gastrointestinal endoscopy at two medical institutions. For esophagogastroduodenoscopies (EGDs) and colonoscopies (CSs), the per‐procedure value represents an aggregate estimate calculated as (the total waste across all the measurement days)/(the total number of procedures across all the measurement days). For endoscopic submucosal dissections (ESDs) and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatographies (ERCPs), values are presented as the mean ± standard deviation per case (n = 10 for each). The lower block shows the distribution of these values across m measurement days (EGDs and CSs) or n cases (ESDs and ERCPs). The values were calculated from unrounded data and may not sum exactly to the totals.

【TABLE 2 · deo270455-tbl-0002】TABLE 2 Time‐adjusted waste generation and estimated incineration‐related CO2 emissions per gastrointestinal endoscopy. The aggregate rate was calculated as (the total waste mass or total estimated CO2 emissions)/(the total procedure duration in minutes) across all the measurements and is retained as the principal estimate; it is an aggregate ratio and is not the mean of the case‐ or day‐level rate. Case‐ and day‐level rates are day‐level values for esophagogastroduodenoscopies (EGDs) and colonoscopies (CSs) (the daily total divided by the total procedure duration that day across m measurement days) and case‐level values for endoscopic submucosal dissections (ESDs) and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatographies (ERCPs) (across n procedures). The duration of each procedure was recorded in all four groups; for EGDs and CSs, only the waste measurements were pooled by day.
